predecessors.name: Nguyễn dynasty (Đại Nam)
predecessors.text: Saigon (1859), then Biên Hòa, Gia Định, Định Tường and Poulo Condore (1862), the western provinces (1867), Bình Thuận (1883) and the protectorates of Annam and Tonkin (1883)

predecessors.name: Post-Angkor Cambodia
predecessors.text: Norodom's kingdom, without Battambang and Siem Reap, which Siam held until 1907

predecessors.name: Rattanakosin Kingdom (Siam)
predecessors.text: the east bank of the Mekong (1893), Trat and Koh Kong (1904), later Battambang, Siem Reap and Banteay Meanchey (1907)

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Luang Phrabang
predecessors.text: Luang Prabang, a protectorate by the page's 1889 bill or 1893 treaty

ledger.x: 1859: the French take Saigon, their first hold in Indochina.
1859: Saigon is occupied, not yet ceded.
1862: the occupation of Saigon becomes cession.
1862: the Treaty of Saigon cedes three provinces and Poulo Condore to France.
1863: Cambodia becomes a French protectorate.
1867: France takes the western provinces of the Mekong delta.
1871: the conquered provinces are organised as the colony of Cochinchina, with Admiral Dupré as first governor; the infobox lists Saigon as capital from 1862.
1883: Bình Thuận is annexed to Cochinchina.
1883: Annam and Tonkin become French protectorates.
1884: French and Chinese troops fight in Tonkin.
1885: China gives up Tonkin.
1887: Cochinchina, Annam, Tonkin and Cambodia are united as French Indochina.
7 April 1889: the Sipsong Chau Tai pass to French Tonkin.
1893: French columns take the east bank of the Mekong from Siam.
1893: the war ends with the treaty.
1893: Siam cedes the east bank of the Mekong, which becomes French Laos.
1893: Laos becomes a French protectorate.
1893: France occupies Chanthaburi as a guarantee.
1900: Guangzhouwan is added to Indochina.
1904: Siam cedes the west-bank lands to French Laos and Cambodia.
1904: Siam gives Trat and Koh Kong to French Indochina.
1904: France gives Chanthaburi back.
1904: Champasak is annexed.
1907: Trat goes back to Siam.
1907: Siam cedes Battambang, Siem Reap and Banteay Meanchey to Cambodia.
1940: Japan enters northern Indochina.
1941: Thailand attacks Laos and Cambodia.
1941: the Tokyo treaty cedes the Cambodian provinces to Thailand.
1941: the Tokyo treaty cedes two Lao provinces to Thailand.
1941: the war ends in Japanese-dictated cession.
1941: Japan occupies southern Indochina.
1945: Guangzhouwan goes back to China.
1945: Japan ends French rule in Cambodia.
1945: Japan ends French rule in Annam and Tonkin.
1945: Luang Prabang breaks with France.
1945: Japan surrenders.
1945: the Japanese leave southern Indochina with the surrender of 15 August 1945; British forces took the south and Chinese forces the north up to the 16th parallel in September.
1945: the Democratic Republic of Vietnam is proclaimed.
1945: the French retake the south.
1945: the French protectorate of Cambodia is re-established.
1946: the French return to the north on terms.
April 1946: the French return to Laos.
1946: Thailand returns the 1941 provinces.
1946: the Ho-Sainteny arrangement breaks down.
1946: the First Indochina War begins.
1949: the State of Vietnam is formed within the French Union.
1953: Laos becomes independent.
1953: Cambodia becomes independent.
1954: the State of Vietnam gains full independence.
1954: the war ends at Geneva.
1954: French Indochina ends.

wars.name: Cochinchina campaign
wars.outcome: The French took Saigon on 17 February 1859 but held only its perimeter; the Treaty of Saigon (5 June 1862) ceded Biên Hòa, Gia Định, Định Tường and Poulo Condore.

wars.name: Sino-French War
wars.outcome: The Tientsin treaty of 9 June 1885 'forced China to abandon its historic claim to suzerainty over Vietnam' and confirmed the French protectorate over Annam and Tonkin.

wars.name: Franco-Siamese War
wars.outcome: Siam ceded the east bank of the Mekong by the Franco-Siamese Treaty of 3 October 1893; Chantaburi was occupied temporarily and Battambang and Siem Reap demilitarised.

wars.name: Japanese invasion of French Indochina
wars.outcome: Japan entered on 22 September 1940, took the Đồng Đăng post and besieged Lạng Sơn, which surrendered four days later; the Vichy administration stayed in place under Japanese garrison.

wars.name: Franco-Thai War
wars.outcome: Thai armies overran Laos and western Cambodia from 5 January 1941; the ceasefire was 28 January and the Tokyo peace treaty of 9 May 1941 forced the French to give up the border provinces to Thailand; they were returned in November 1946.

wars.name: First Indochina War
wars.outcome: Hostilities began on 19 December 1946 and ended with the fall of Dien Bien Phu on 7 May 1954 and the Geneva Accords of 21 July 1954, which divided Vietnam at the 17th parallel.

certainty.note: Cochinchina's provinces and Cambodia's protectorate are named without boundaries on the pages; Tonkin was not pacified (the page: about ten further years from 1886).

Treaty frontiers: the Sino-Vietnamese border was demarcated in 1887, the Mekong frontier by the treaties of 1893, 1904 and 1907 and the Laos-Burma border by the treaty with Britain in 1896; the interior of Laos and the Annamite highlands…
The Thai-held provinces of 1941-1946, the Japanese occupation, the Chinese and British zones of 1945-46 and the Viet Minh zones of 1946-1954 are approximate.
